## Decision so far

The fixed-model comparison does not support adopting an ML adjustment yet.
All four classifiers have weak loss-probability performance, and none improves
on the historical loss-frequency control on Brier score or log loss. Portfolio
effects vary by the underlying trading rule.

This is a reproducible research draft, not the final submission conclusion.
A final feature choice, hyperparameter tuning, a final strategy choice and
the official frozen-training test comparison remain to be completed.

## Comparison design

The experiment compares thirteen original portfolios and fifty-two adjusted
versions over the same January 2005–December 2009 earned-return window. Initial
history comes from the first sixty training snapshots. Each classifier uses the
same twenty original factors and the same annual expanding fit dates. The
non-ML portfolio rules and probability-to-weight adjustment are held fixed.

These are training-period validation results. The previously viewed test period
is not a fresh holdout. The final test model fits will use the separate
frozen-at-origin policy, rather than learning from earlier test labels.

## Predictive quality

Lower Brier score and log loss indicate better probability estimates. ROC AUC
measures ranking and is not, by itself, evidence of useful portfolio returns.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-predictors
#| tbl-cap: "Fixed classifiers against a historical loss-frequency control."
display(predictive_table(summary).style.format({"Brier score": "{:.6f}", "Log loss": "{:.6f}", "ROC AUC": "{:.4f}"}))
```

## Portfolio outcomes

The following portfolios illustrate the effect of applying each model to the
same trading rule. The complete saved result contains all 65 portfolio cases.
Returns are gross of transaction costs; every portfolio is long-only and fully
invested. The model changes relative stock weights, not total market exposure.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-cagr
#| tbl-cap: "Matched-window CAGR by model and portfolio rule."
display(portfolio_table(summary).style.format("{:.2%}"))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-portfolios
#| fig-cap: "Growth of an initial dollar and drawdown for original and model-adjusted portfolios."
figure = portfolio_figure(summary)
display(figure)
plt.close(figure)
```

## Equal-weight accounting reference

This independent reference covers the full supplied train and test return
windows, unlike the shorter model-validation comparison above. Each month's
portfolio return is the arithmetic average of stock simple returns. These
portfolio returns are then compounded through time. Averaging stock log returns
would produce a different, incorrect equal-capital portfolio calculation.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-equal-weight
#| tbl-cap: "Full-window equal-weight accounting reference from Part 0."
display(benchmark_table().style.format({"Months": "{:.0f}", "CAGR": "{:.2%}", "Volatility": "{:.2%}", "Sharpe": "{:.3f}", "Max drawdown": "{:.2%}"}))
```

## Feature selection: four matched recipes

This is a separately pinned training study, with all fourteen current portfolio
rules, four fixed pooled downside classifiers, annual expanding fits and the
same January 2005–December 2009 earned months. The cash-capable annual-consistency
rule uses three-month momentum. All recipes use adjustment strength 0.50. This
study has 280 portfolio cases across four runs; the earlier thirteen-rule
comparison above remains its own recorded experiment.

```{python}
#| label: feature-study-protocol
from IPython.display import Markdown
from research.feature_reporting import (
    method_notes, importance_table, importance_figure, selection_overlap,
    prediction_summary, portfolio_table as feature_portfolio_table,
    portfolio_figure as feature_portfolio_figure, forest_findings,
)
feature_study = summary.get("feature_study")
if feature_study is None:
    display(Markdown("No feature study is pinned in this release."))
else:
    display(Markdown(method_notes()))
    display(pd.DataFrame([{"Recipe": key, "Saved run": value}
                         for key, value in feature_study["metadata"]["runs"].items()]))
```

### Forest importance and selected inputs

The chart uses the first historical training fit, before the displayed
validation returns were earned. The selector forest and downstream predictor
have separate jobs. Bar lengths measure training split importance; error bars
show standard deviation across trees, not confidence intervals. Correlated
factors can share importance. Financial interpretations of the supplied factors
remain available in the data dictionary and the app.

```{python}
#| label: fig-forest-importance
#| fig-cap: "Forest selection from twenty candidates at the first historical origin; highlighted factors are retained."
if feature_study is not None:
    figure = importance_figure(feature_study)
    display(figure)
    plt.close(figure)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-forest-selected
#| tbl-cap: "Actual selected factors and overlap between selection methods at the first fit."
if feature_study is not None:
    selected = importance_table(feature_study)
    display(selected.loc[selected.selected, ["feature", "group", "meaning", "rank", "score", "importance_std"]].round(6))
    display(selection_overlap(feature_study))
```

### Effects after retraining

Every classifier was independently refitted for each recipe at every origin.
Selection and scaling see only then-known outcomes. Non-ML rules remain
identical across recipes. Lower Brier score and log loss are better; selected
recipes should also be compared against the historical event-frequency control.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-feature-prediction
#| tbl-cap: "Four fixed predictors across all twenty, ANOVA, pruning and forest-selected recipes."
if feature_study is not None:
    display(Markdown(forest_findings(feature_study)))
    display(prediction_summary(feature_study)[[
        "model_id", "recipe", "brier_score", "log_loss", "roc_auc",
        "Brier change vs all 20", "Log-loss change vs all 20",
    ]].round(6))
```

The following portfolio example uses the same logistic predictor and
annual-consistency/momentum/cash trading rule for all four recipes. Cash earns
an assumed zero return; results are gross of costs. A favorable portfolio row
does not establish useful forecasting. The app and exported tables cover all
fourteen rules and all four predictors.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-feature-portfolios
#| tbl-cap: "Matched feature recipes: logistic overlay on the three-month momentum/cash rule."
if feature_study is not None:
    display(feature_portfolio_table(feature_study, "logistic", ["annual_consistency_momentum_cash"])[[
        "recipe", "cagr", "annualized_log_growth", "sharpe", "sortino", "max_drawdown",
        "avg_one_way_turnover", "avg_cash_weight", "change_cagr_vs_all20",
    ]].round(6))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-feature-log-returns
#| fig-cap: "Saved cumulative portfolio log returns and drawdowns; unchanged non-ML reference shown once."
if feature_study is not None:
    figure = feature_portfolio_figure(feature_study, cumulative_log=True)
    display(figure)
    plt.close(figure)
```

### Separate tuning evidence and pending final evaluation

Annual selected-feature unions may exceed ten; each fitted selected model uses
at most ten. A frozen final model must choose its inputs once before evaluation.
This feature study uses fixed model settings. A separate saved tuning holdout
comparison is available in the app for logistic regression and histogram
boosting; it uses a different January 2007–December 2009 window and is not part
of this pinned feature comparison. A forest-selected tuned comparison, final
specification and official frozen-training test result remain pending.

## Data and reproducibility

A row describes one stock at a month-end snapshot. Its forward return belongs
to the following month. Source data, derived input timing, parameters, runtime
versions and result identities are recorded in the pinned artifact's manifest.
Rendering this document loads saved results; it does not train models or run a
parameter search.

```{python}
display(pd.DataFrame([{"Property": name, "Value": str(value)} for name, value in {
    "Pinned run": summary["run_id"],
    "Source splits": summary["data_audit"]["source_splits"],
    "First earned month": summary["data_audit"]["first_return_month"],
    "Last earned month": summary["data_audit"]["last_return_month"],
    "Evaluation rows": summary["data_audit"]["evaluation_rows"],
    "Model training policy": summary["manifest"]["config"].get("fit_policy", "expanding"),
}.items()]))
```
